solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pack case for accordion

parts.note: to pack is to cram or squeeze things in
a box is a case or container

explanation.surface: Someone packing away a musical instrument in its carrying case.
explanation.definitionFit: Squeezebox is the informal name for the bellows instrument played by squeezing and pulling.

clue.text: Question abnormal autumn amount

indicators.note: abnormal means out of the usual order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone querying an unusually large figure for the autumn.
explanation.definitionFit: A quantum is a quantity or share, especially a fixed portion of something.

clue.text: Incident in flat ending in arrest

parts.note: a flat, level surface is even

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its final letter, taken from the word arrest

explanation.surface: A police report of something that happened in an apartment and led to an arrest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' looks like a home, but here it is the adjective meaning level.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is an occurrence or happening, which is what an incident is.

clue.text: One of Groucho's brothers almost landed on river, going north in airship

indicators.note: in a down entry, landing on something means sitting on top of it, so the brother's name comes first
almost means not quite whole, so the final letter of the brother's name is dropped

parts.note: Zeppo was one of the Marx Brothers alongside Groucho

indicators.note: in a down clue, going north means reading upwards, so the river's name is written backwards

parts.note: the Nile is the great river of Egypt

explanation.surface: A Marx brother nearly touching down on a river in a dirigible.
explanation.definitionFit: A Zeppelin is a rigid airship of the type built by Count von Zeppelin.

clue.text: Have bellboy call, different game being required

indicators.note: different means changed in form, so these letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A hotel guest asks for the porter to be summoned because a different sport is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Beach volleyball is a sport played on sand, a variety of the team game.

clue.text: Kane's estate secured by Texan, a dude

indicators.note: something secured by these words is held within them, so the letters are found inside the phrase

explanation.surface: A cowboy-booted Texan buys a grand property.
explanation.walkthrough: Kane is Charles Foster Kane, the tycoon in the film Citizen Kane.
explanation.definitionFit: In Citizen Kane, Kane's vast Florida palace and grounds are named after the pleasure-dome of Coleridge's poem.

clue.text: Shrewd signal saving time

indicators.note: saving here means keeping safe inside, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a cue is a signal to an actor to begin

explanation.surface: A canny gesture that cuts down the time taken.
explanation.definitionFit: Cute in its older, chiefly American sense means clever or sharp-witted, as in a cute move.

clue.text: Winner, Ms Grey, mostly bubbly?

parts.note: a champ, short for champion, is a winner

indicators.note: mostly means most of it, so the name's last letter is dropped

parts.note: Agnes Grey is the title heroine of Anne Brontë's novel

explanation.surface: A query whether a victorious woman named Grey is largely cheerful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bubbly' reads as a personality, but it is the noun for fizzy wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Bubbly is the informal word for sparkling wine, most famously the French one from Reims and Épernay.

clue.text: Proposition made by Greek boy band?

parts.note: Theo is a boy's name of Greek origin, from the word for god
REM is an American rock band

explanation.surface: A suggestion apparently dreamt up by a boy band from Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: A proposition in mathematics or logic is a statement to be proved, which is a theorem.

clue.text: Jack plug taken by English hack

parts.note: J is the card-playing abbreviation for jack
a plug is a promotion, an ad

explanation.surface: An electrical jack plug borrowed by a British journalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hack' looks like a writer, but here it is an old horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A jade is a worn-out, broken-down horse, which is also the old meaning of a hack.

clue.text: No lines on me in FT, say, after I invested in scheme

indicators.note: after places the newspaper piece behind the scheme piece
invested in means put into, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a plan is a scheme
the Financial Times is an example of a newspaper

explanation.surface: A complaint that the newspaper has given someone no column space after a financial investment.
explanation.definitionFit: Unruled writing sheets carry no printed lines, and that is what this stationery term describes, speaking for itself.

clue.text: Cast figure, standing, not right

indicators.note: not means without, so a letter is taken out

parts.note: stature is standing or reputation

explanation.surface: A figure in a play stands up, though not correctly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast figure' suggests a character in a play; here it is a figure cast in bronze.
explanation.definitionFit: A statue is a sculpted figure, often cast in metal from a mould.

clue.text: Prayed uneasily in heart of Tashkent and here, in London

indicators.note: uneasily means unsettled, so the letters are thrown into a new order
the heart of a word is its central part, here the two middle letters of Tashkent

explanation.surface: A worshipper prays nervously in central Uzbekistan and then in London.
explanation.walkthrough: Hyde Park is the large royal park in central London.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition points to a place in London; the park is a famous open space there.

clue.text: I met GP for treatment involving one old skin complaint

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the reworked letters hold another piece
something put through treatment is worked over and changed, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A patient seeing a doctor about an old rash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for treatment' rearranges I MET GP to IMPETG, which takes I inside before O is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Impetigo is a contagious bacterial infection of the skin causing sores and crusts.

clue.text: Questioning former Ugandan dictator in Ghana's capital

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
Idi Amin ruled Uganda as dictator in the 1970s

indicators.note: a capital letter is the initial one, so the first letter of the country's name is taken

explanation.surface: A former African tyrant being interrogated in the Ghanaian capital, Accra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' tempts towards Accra, but it only means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Examining someone means asking them questions, as a lawyer does a witness.

clue.text: Doctor holding a male's umbrella

indicators.note: holding means keeping inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A doctor carrying a man's brolly.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamp is a British word for a large umbrella, after Mrs Gamp, who carried one in Dickens's Martin Chuzzlewit.

clue.text: Flower at present lying in small ditch

indicators.note: lying in means resting within, so this piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to ditch something is to drop it
at present means now

explanation.surface: A bloom currently growing in a little roadside trench.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ditch' looks like a noun for a trench but works as the verb meaning abandon.
explanation.definitionFit: The snowdrop is a small white bulb plant that blooms in late winter.

clue.text: Unsatisfactory, a king of Mercia

parts.note: off means below standard, as in an off day

explanation.surface: A judgment that a certain Anglo-Saxon ruler was a disappointment.
explanation.walkthrough: Mercia was an Anglo-Saxon kingdom in the English Midlands; its king built the earthwork known as his Dyke.
explanation.definitionFit: Offa was the eighth-century ruler of the Midlands realm of Mercia.

clue.text: Hotchpotch in Portuguese resort shown round daily, perhaps

indicators.note: shown round means placed around, so the resort's letters go about the other piece

parts.note: Faro is a resort town on Portugal's Algarve coast
a daily newspaper is an example of a rag, slang for a paper

explanation.surface: A mixed bag of a tour round a Portuguese holiday town, perhaps every day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'daily' suggests a frequency; it is a newspaper, and a disreputable paper is a rag.
explanation.definitionFit: A farrago is a confused mixture or jumble, the same as a hotchpotch.

clue.text: Passenger ship that is stocking good underwear

indicators.note: stocking means keeping in stock, holding within, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: a liner is a large passenger ship
ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A cruise ship's shop stocks quality nightwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stocking' looks like hosiery in this underwear surface, but it means holding.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingerie is women's underclothing and nightwear.

clue.text: Bad carrying on with a criminal

indicators.note: carrying means bearing within, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: ill means bad, as in ill luck
on is the leg side in cricket, so on gives leg

explanation.surface: A wicked crook carrying on with an accomplice.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the on side is also called the leg side, the half of the field behind the batter's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Criminal as an adjective means against the law, unlawful.

clue.text: Remained sober, by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it signals a word that is pronounced the same as another

parts.note: staid means sober, sedate

explanation.surface: Someone stayed clear-headed, or so it seemed from what was heard.
explanation.definitionFit: Remained and stayed both mean continued in place, the past tense of stay.

clue.text: Sitar playing — hear genius

indicators.note: playing means moving about freely, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: to hear a case in court is to try it

explanation.surface: Listen to a virtuoso playing the sitar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hear' looks like listening, but in a courtroom sense it means try.
explanation.definitionFit: Artistry is creative skill of a high order, the gift a genius shows.

clue.text: WI member appearing with the French nun's headdress

parts.note: WI is the Women's Institute, a British women's community organisation, taken as written
an MP is a Member of Parliament
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A Women's Institute member turns up with a nun's veil from France.
explanation.definitionFit: A wimple is a cloth covering the head, neck and sides of the face, worn by some nuns.

clue.text: Parody of opera heroine, cold

parts.note: Mimi is the heroine of Puccini's La Bohème
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A spoof of a chilly operatic leading lady.
explanation.walkthrough: Mimi famously sings of her tiny frozen hand, so 'cold' fits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To parody someone is to imitate them, often for comic effect, which is to mimic.

clue.text: Book produced by Italian in navy, awfully objective

indicators.note: in signals one piece placed inside another
awfully means badly, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: It is short for Italian, as in It vermouth
fair means objective, impartial

explanation.surface: A book written by an Italian sailor, terribly impartial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' seems to modify 'objective' but scrambles the word before it, giving VANY; 'objective' is the adjective meaning impartial, not a goal.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanity Fair is Thackeray's novel featuring Becky Sharp.

clue.text: Very large jewel brought over by American

indicators.note: brought over means turned over, so the jewel word is read backwards

parts.note: a gem is a jewel

explanation.surface: A huge gemstone shipped across by someone from the US.
explanation.definitionFit: Mega is an informal word for huge or enormous.

clue.text: Moving after I lost medal

indicators.note: lost means gone missing, so the letter is removed

parts.note: going means moving

explanation.surface: An emotional speech after someone failed to win a decoration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving' suggests touching; it means in motion.
explanation.definitionFit: Gong is British slang for a medal or award.

clue.text: Relish last of salad? Unfortunate dilemma

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter, taken from salad

parts.note: ill means unlucky, as in ill fortune
a pickle is a predicament or dilemma

explanation.surface: A sad quandary over the final scraps of salad and whether to enjoy them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relish' looks like a verb for enjoying; it is the noun for a condiment.
explanation.definitionFit: A pickled cucumber flavoured with the herb is served as a tangy relish.
